# CamX Tripod Carrier Board (rev A)

A two-layer carrier board (160 x 62 mm) that replaces the jumper-wire power and signal wiring
of the tripod. Open `Tripod circuit.kicad_pro` in KiCad 7 or later.

**Status: first draft, not fabricated or tested.** The schematic and PCB were generated by
script and autorouted (Freerouting). KiCad's design rule check reports no clearance errors and
no unconnected pads, and the PCB netlist matches the schematic. Review the items under
"Check before ordering" first.

## What it changes, and why

| Problem on the current rig | What the board does |
|---|---|
| ESP32 browned out and dropped Wi-Fi when the servos moved; everything shared one 5 V regulator | One 5 V / 3 A buck regulator per servo (U2, U3), each with its own input, output and servo-side bulk capacitors. The ESP32's 5 V is taken through a Schottky diode (D3) with its own 470 uF hold-up capacitor (C9), so a servo dip cannot pull it down |
| The INA219 module's 0.1 ohm shunt and jumper contacts starved the regulator | INA219 on the board with a 10 mOhm shunt (R2), Kelvin-connected through a 10 R / 100 nF input filter (R8, R9, C13) |
| Miswiring the INA219 destroyed an ESP32 board | Fixed traces, a reverse-polarity MOSFET on the battery input (Q1), and a 6.3 A fuse (F1) |
| Nothing stops the tilt axis driving into its end stop | Two limit-switch inputs (J7, J8) on GPIO10 and GPIO11 |
| No power switch | Terminal J2 for an external switch in series with the battery (rated 6 A or more) |

Also on the board: I2C expansion header (J9), power LED (D4), four M3 mounting holes, and a
copper keep-out under the DevKit's antenna.

## Test points

Loop test points for a multimeter or scope clip, each labelled on the silkscreen:

| Test point | Net | Expect |
|---|---|---|
| TP1 `VRAW` | Battery at the input terminal, before the fuse and switch | 6.0-8.4 V |
| TP2 `VBAT` | Battery after the fuse, switch, MOSFET and shunt (regulator input) | within about 0.1 V of TP1 under load |
| TP3 `5V PAN` | Pan servo regulator output | 5.0 V |
| TP4 `5V TILT` | Tilt servo regulator output | 5.0 V |
| TP5 `5V LOG` | ESP32 5 V supply, after the isolation diode | about 4.7 V |
| TP6 `GND` | Ground reference | 0 V |

The difference between TP1 and TP2 under load is the drop across the whole protection chain.

## Signals

| Function | ESP32-C6 pin | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Pan servo PWM | GPIO2 | via 220 R (R5) to J5 pin 3 |
| Tilt servo PWM | GPIO3 | via 220 R (R6) to J6 pin 3 |
| I2C SDA / SCL | GPIO6 / GPIO7 | INA219 at 0x40, 4k7 pull-ups to 3V3 |
| Limit switch up / down | GPIO10 / GPIO11 | switch to GND, use the internal pull-up |

These match `firmware/camx_tripod/camx_tripod.ino`. Servo headers are GND, +5 V, signal.

## Firmware changes this board needs

- **INA219 calibration.** The Adafruit library's default calibration assumes a 0.1 ohm shunt.
  With 10 mOhm the reported current is ten times too low until the calibration (or a x10
  scale factor) is changed.
- **Limit switches.** The firmware does not read GPIO10/11 yet.

## Check before ordering

1. **DevKit pinout and row spacing.** J3/J4 assume an ESP32-C6-DevKitC-1: two rows of 16
   pins, 22.86 mm apart, with the pin order on the schematic. Measure your board and compare
   its silkscreen pin by pin; other ESP32-C6 boards differ.
2. **Screw terminal orientation.** Confirm in the 3D viewer that the wire entries of J1 and J2
   face the board edge, and rotate them if not.
3. **Regulator headroom.** The LM2596 needs about 1.3 V more than its output at full load, so
   the 5 V rails start to sag below a pack voltage of roughly 6.5 V. The MG996R runs down to
   4.8 V, so this costs speed, not function.
4. **Current rating.** Battery-path traces are 1.5 mm and servo-rail traces 1.0 mm, the widest
   the autorouter could fit between the regulator pins. In 1 oz copper that suits the rig's
   normal draw but runs warm at the 6.3 A fuse rating or a sustained 3 A servo stall. Order
   2 oz copper, or widen the long runs by hand.
5. **Regulator layout.** The autorouter does not know that the input capacitor, regulator and
   diode of a buck converter should form a tight loop. It works at the LM2596's 150 kHz, but
   tidying that loop by hand will reduce noise.
6. **Library notices.** A design rule check run without KiCad's footprint libraries configured
   lists 52 "footprint does not match library" notices; they are not layout errors.

The schematic uses net labels rather than drawn wires between blocks. `Tripod circuit
schematic.pdf`, `board-front.png` and `board-back.png` are exports of this revision.

## Production files

`production/` was generated with the Fabrication Toolkit plugin (bennymeg/Fabrication-Toolkit),
using its JLCPCB rotation corrections:

- `Tripod_circuit.zip` -- gerbers and drill files, ready to upload
- `bom.csv` -- bill of materials in JLCPCB's format
- `positions.csv` -- component placement file
- `designators.csv`, `netlist.ipc`

The "LCSC Part #" column in `bom.csv` is empty: no LCSC part numbers have been chosen. It only
matters if JLCPCB assembles the board; fill it in after picking parts that are in stock.
Regenerate these files after any change to the board.
